nodes.label: Pure TypeScript Simulation Engine
nodes.rationale: Engine is pure TypeScript with zero browser dependencies (no DOM, window, canvas, localStorage). Runs in Web Worker (single-player) or Node.js (multiplayer) — same code, different transport adapter. This makes multiplayer a bolt-on, not a rewrite.

nodes.label: Transport Adapter Pattern
nodes.rationale: Engine communicates via SimTransport interface. PostMessageTransport for single-player, WebSocketTransport for multiplayer. Engine never touches postMessage, WebSocket, or any I/O directly. Only host/ and transport/ differ between single-player and multiplayer.

nodes.label: Multiplayer-Ready Architecture
nodes.rationale: Adding multiplayer requires: write WebSocketTransport (~50 lines), write server-host.ts (~100 lines), add server package. Zero changes to engine code. Engine uses seeded RNG (PCG32) for deterministic replays.

nodes.label: PixiJS v8 Rendering Engine
nodes.rationale: WebGL/WebGPU GPU rendering guarantees performance at any network scale (50k+ sprites at 60fps). Engine decoupled from renderer via transport layer. Editor interactions require manual implementation (spatial hashing, custom event handlers) but this is a one-time cost concentrated in Milestones 3–5.

nodes.label: React-UI Rendering Separation
nodes.rationale: React only manages UI chrome (toolbars, panels, dialogs, HUD). PixiJS mutates sprites directly via imperative game-loop pattern. Simulation state flows directly from Worker to PixiJS via transport layer, never through React state. Zustand used for UI-only state, simulation state bypasses React entirely.
